title: Research: exact restoration contracts and resource bounds for rounded borrowing
body:
[PR #1057](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1057) proves exact restoration with three dirty arrays when every child is additive. The rounded leaves from [PR #985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/985) and the precision proof in [PR #1054](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1054) do not supply that contract. This package identifies the actual borrowed boundary and proves its necessary and sufficient translation condition.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4c35687d7c0da8e6cf33f17e418ecf31c95ff3ad/research/rounded-borrowing-contract/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4c35687d7c0da8e6cf33f17e418ecf31c95ff3ad/research/rounded-borrowing-contract/VALIDATION.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4c35687d7c0da8e6cf33f17e418ecf31c95ff3ad/research/rounded-borrowing-contract/SOURCES.json).

The result is a scoped obstruction and resource tradeoff. It makes no new kappa claim.

- An exact additive wrapper on the same arbitrary fine grid has integer slope. It cannot approximate the valid [PR #985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/985) map `x -> 4x/3` with error below `1/3` on the physical interval `[-1,1]`, even with more guard bits or unlimited restored workspace. Restricted source grids and different output grids are explicit escapes.
- For componentwise nearest rounding of `Pz/q`, the safe translations are exactly `Ph=0 mod q`. A correction that cannot reread the old helper needs one saved state per quotient class. For a coprime scalar on L entries this gives `q^L` states when the admitted source and displacement ranges contain a complete residue domain. Smaller finite domains can need fewer states. Readable current data and displacement can recover the old helper without a saved summary; the proof accounts for that escape at the actual borrowing boundary.
- A nonzero additive result from fixed signed offset averaging needs at least q variable calls. The matching q-call construction returns the q-scaled integer map. A separate exact integer lift pays for denominator growth, initialized low bits, all local operations, source access, and inverse calls. It is a comparison construction, not a fast rounded supplier.

The written proof is supported by deterministic exact checks: 716 reduced scalar ratios, 3,495,180 residue responses, all 700 normalized functions on cyclic groups of orders 2 through 5 at the emitted child boundary, six matrix quotients, 380 pinned rounded leaf executions, 22 finite exact lifts, and nine mathematical controls. A read-only relocated replay under optimized Python passes. Three real subprocess controls reject a changed pinned source, a discarded residue, and an occupied output file.

Reproduce from the repository root with the Python standard library:

```sh
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1 python3 -I -B research/rounded-borrowing-contract/test_package.py
```

Expected final markers:

```text
PASS_ROUNDED_BORROWING_CONTRACT ratios=716 responses=3495180 rounded_leaves=380 exact_lifts=22 controls=9
PASS_ROUNDED_BORROWING_PACKAGE controls=3 relocation=1
```

The selected-record check and all 25 selected unit tests passed on the exact experiment base. Full `make verify`, the selected cold replay, remote CI, and a physical tape compiler were not run. This change only adds the isolated research package. Finite replay is not a formal proof of the full multiplication theorem.

Experiment base: [abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf). Source pins: [PR #1057](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1057) [78a062df1dcab2bffea5ff4d8243f3da6e465414](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/78a062df1dcab2bffea5ff4d8243f3da6e465414); [PR #985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/985) [da1cdf8ed4ac9b1b8378dfec73f77ff4e81a4f70](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/da1cdf8ed4ac9b1b8378dfec73f77ff4e81a4f70); [PR #1054](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1054) [6bc675be1554b3a3be771147f21f9dc2c6dae50a](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/6bc675be1554b3a3be771147f21f9dc2c6dae50a). The package freezes exact source and context bytes. During the work, main [ba82555c64e1879e4b7decce28186f208fcb8262](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/ba82555c64e1879e4b7decce28186f208fcb8262) selected [PR #1042](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1042) at conditional `kappa=1672188119205421/10^18`; this package does not alter that selection or any supplier call moment.

The proof, failed approaches, finite domains, overlap checks, and validation receipt are in [research/rounded-borrowing-contract/](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/4c35687d7c0da8e6cf33f17e418ecf31c95ff3ad/research/rounded-borrowing-contract). It credits Gareth Davidson (@bitplane)'s [PR #1057](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1057) and the retained predecessor lineage. Prepared for Ali Romman (@aliromman) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in the research, proof, implementation, verification, and text. New material is Apache-2.0. No independent human or proof-assistant review is claimed.
